newsitem.title: USA: Russia meat imports to remain 2 mln tonnes--USDA.
newsitem.headline: Russia meat imports to remain 2 mln tonnes--USDA.

text.p: Russian meat imports from outside the former Soviet Union are likely to remain about 2 million tonnes annually over the next several years, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Wednesday.
In its annual report on agriculture in the former Soviet Union, USDA said about half of the projected meat imports would be poultry -- with 80 percent coming from the United States.
However, the European Union, which captured about 20 percent of the market in 1996, "continues to slowly increase its position," USDA said.
The EU already dominates Russian imports of beef from outside the former Soviet Union. It supplies about 80 percent, compared to China in second place with 10 percent.
Meanwhile, China supplies about 50 percent of Russia's imports of pork from outside the former Soviet, followed by Eastern Europe which has about 25 percent of that market.
During the days of the USSR, about 40 percent of Russian meat imports came from its fellow Soviet republics. But that has now fallen to about 15 percent, USDA said.

The United States, EU and China have been able to increase market share as a result of economic reforms throughout the former Soviet Union that have exposed the inefficiencies of the region's meat production system, USDA said.
Imports accounted for about 53 percent of Russian poultry consumption in 1996, compared to only 5 pct in 1991.
Over the same period, imports have risen to 23 percent of Russian pork consumption from 7 percent; and to 18 percent of Russian beef consumption from 15 percent, USDA said.
